arcs.title: Dana: Haifa
arcs.stage: Wed Nov 25 (midpoint): Lior let Haifa slip; 'congratulations' twice. Thu Nov 26: 'I want you to stay' to a pretend barista in improv, then 'Busy Friday. Sorry.' to Dana, Tomer read it over his shoulder. Fri Nov 27 (week 3): he stays away from Cafe Nahat; Avi says she asked if he was sick; Noa calls it what it is: apologising by disappearing. Next: Sun Dec 6 he says it plainly.

arcs.title: Gadi: Unpaid
arcs.stage: Tue Nov 24: 'Thursday payment run confirmed!!'. Thu Nov 26: the run 'went out', Sababa's batch is Monday; Ishai asks for Monday before ten in writing and refuses the Hebrew banner until then. Next: week 3 Gadi asks for January and Ishai gets angry for the first time.
arcs.secret: Sababa Creative lost its biggest client in October. Gadi is paying every freelancer late and hides it behind cheerful 'small things'.

arcs.title: Noa: Shir
arcs.stage: Thu Nov 26: came with a duffel at 18:49 and left again, burekas in the hallway at 21:03, then skipped the night out, 'dead tired'. Fri Nov 27: drops by with a challah, tells him he is disappearing, won't talk about her phone ('tomorrow is about you'). Next: Sat Nov 28 after havdalah, dinner just them: he finds out, and for once takes care of her.
arcs.secret: Noa's girlfriend of three years, Shir, moved out in October. Noa told nobody: it's why she is late, cancels plans and pushes Ishai's love life so hard.

arcs.title: Mrs. Levi and Eli
arcs.stage: Thu Nov 26 (reveal): four years since Eli came; 'busy is easier than far'; Ishai promised not to CALL. Fri Nov 27: he writes to Eli instead (a text, not a call), two grey ticks; Shabbat dinner with Mrs. Levi, who says Eli used to call every Friday before candles. His phone buzzes face down during dinner and he leaves it. Next: Eli lands Mon Nov 30.
arcs.secret: Mrs. Levi is lonely: her son Eli in Toronto hasn't visited in four years, and she always says he's busy.

arcs.title: Avi's kiosk
arcs.stage: Thu Nov 26 (reveal): the envelope, double rent from January; Avi pushed his kiosk keys on Ishai and left for the afternoon. Fri Nov 27: Avi takes the keys back (he was at his cousin's, the one who 'knows contracts'), refuses Ishai's flyer and then keeps it. Next: week 4 a sufganiyot queue round the block; open.
arcs.secret: Avi's landlord is doubling the kiosk's rent from January.

arcs.title: Improv on Thursdays
arcs.stage: Thu Nov 26, lesson 4, the last Noa paid for: in a scene with a barista who is leaving he says 'I want you to stay' and 'I'll learn the timetable'. He signs up for the next course (from Dec 10) at full price, himself. Yael: 'now the real one'.

arcs.title: Lior's novel and Moshe
arcs.stage: Wed Nov 25: Lior let Haifa slip and called himself a fool; 'chapter fifteen is ruined'. Moshe: fewer aphids. Next: Sun Nov 29 Ishai reads chapter one for the cover and recognises himself.
arcs.secret: Lior's novel is about Ishai: 'the man who apologises to his coffee'.

arcs.title: Tomer and Noa
arcs.stage: Thu Nov 26: beers and pool at The Black Candle; read 'Busy Friday. Sorry.' over Ishai's shoulder and told Noa. Sat Nov 28: PixelPlex with Ishai (A Midsummer Night's Dream, 21:00, engine). Next: showing up for Noa.
arcs.secret: Tomer has liked Noa since school.

arcs.title: The poker table
arcs.stage: First night Mon Nov 23: 91 up. Tue Nov 24 Ishai lent Yossi 200, 'don't tell Boaz'. Next: second night Mon Dec 7, Yossi pays back in coins.

beats.goal: Friday morning on Herzl Street. Ishai brings Avi's kiosk keys back (Avi pushed them on him yesterday and vanished for the afternoon). Avi is sheepish: he spent the day at his cousin Shimon's, who 'knows contracts' and knew nothing. Ishai shows him the flyer he drafted for the kiosk; Avi says flyers don't pay rent, then folds it into his apron. Avi mentions Dana came by at eight for a falafel and asked if Ishai was sick. Ishai changes the subject. No solution to the rent today.
beats.teaser: Ishai returns Avi's keys. Avi has news he didn't ask for.
beats.forceText: Ishai gives Avi back the kiosk keys. Avi admits the cousin who 'knows contracts' knew nothing, and keeps Ishai's flyer.

forceLines.say: My cousin knows contracts. He knew nothing. Free advice, worth it.
Keep the flyer. Just in case.

forceCommentary.say: A cousin who knows contracts. Every family has one. None of them do.
Dana asked if he was sick. He is. Lovesick and hiding.

moments.text: Friday rush at the kiosk: people with flower bunches queue for pitas. Ishai waits at the end of the counter and puts Avi's keys down, wrapped in yesterday's napkin.

lines.say: Your keys. You left in a hurry.
Ah. The keys. Yes. Thank you, motek.
And you told me to water Moshe.
I said that? I meant the mint. My head was not here.
Where was it?
Ramat Gan. My cousin Shimon. He knows contracts.
And?
He knows nothing. Free advice. Worth every agora.
So the rent is still double.
Double is double. Shimon can't make it single.
Pita? On the house. Today I'm generous, January I'm broke.
I'll pay. That's the whole point, Avi.
Ha! Now you sound like my landlord.
Sorry. No. Not sorry. You know what I mean.
Extra amba. Eat, before you apologise again.
Okay. Thanks.

commentary.say: A cousin who knows contracts. Every family has one. None of them do.
'January I'm broke.' He's smiling. The envelope isn't.

then.text: Ishai eats his pita at the end of the counter while Avi serves three customers in a row without a word.

moments.text: The queue thins. Ishai takes a folded sheet from his pocket: a flyer he drew yesterday, the kiosk with a little sun over it and ELEVEN YEARS ON THIS CORNER. Avi looks at it a long time.

lines.say: I made you something. Yesterday. Don't laugh.
What is this?
A flyer. 'Eleven years on this corner.'
Flyers don't pay rent, champion.
No. But people come. More people, more pitas.
You drew the sun over my kiosk.
It's always sunny on that corner. Mostly.
Hm.
Your barista came by. Eight o'clock. A falafel, half amba.
Okay.
She asked if you were sick.
What did you say?
I said ask him. I'm a falafel man, not a post office.
Can we talk about the flyer?
We talked. It's nice. It doesn't pay rent.
Keep it. Just in case.
Just in case.
Shabbat shalom, Avi.

commentary.say: Dana asked if he was sick. He is. Lovesick and hiding.
He folded it into the apron. That's Avi for 'I love it'.

then.text: Avi folds the flyer twice and slides it into his apron pocket, next to the envelope, without looking at Ishai.

update.memory: Took my keys back from Ishai. Shimon knew nothing. Ishai drew a flyer, 'eleven years on this corner'. I kept it. Told him Dana asked if he was sick.

beats.goal: After his nap. Noa knocks with a challah from the bakery and sunglasses she keeps on indoors. Tomer told her about 'Busy Friday. Sorry.' She calls it what it is: he is apologising by disappearing, the coffee at home, the bad excuse. Ishai pushes back for once and turns it round: her phone, the duffel yesterday, 'dead tired'. She deflects hard: tomorrow's dinner is about him, not her. She leaves before candles, to her parents'. Neither of them wins.
beats.teaser: Noa brings a challah, and a word for what he's doing.
beats.forceText: Noa drops by with a challah and tells Ishai he is apologising by disappearing. He asks about her phone; she won't say.

forceLines.say: You're not busy. You're apologising by disappearing.
And you? The phone, the duffel? Dead tired?

forceCommentary.say: She named it. Disappearing. Write it on the fridge, babe.
Two people telling each other to talk. Neither talking. Classic Friday.

moments.text: A knock. Noa, sunglasses on although the stairwell is dark, holding a braided challah in a paper bag. She walks past him straight to the counter.

lines.say: Challah. Sesame. You're welcome.
You can take the sunglasses off. It's indoors.
I like them. Tomer called me.
Tomer calls everybody.
'Busy Friday. Sorry.' Really, Ishai?
He read it over my shoulder. That's not—
Are you busy? Look at me. Are you busy?
I have a banner. And Shabbat. And—
And a coffee machine you hate.
I don't hate it. It hates me.
You haven't been to Nahat in two days.
Three. Not that I'm counting.
You're counting. That's the worst part.
You know what you're doing? Apologising. By disappearing.
That's not a thing.
It's your whole thing. Since school.

commentary.say: She named it. Disappearing. Write it on the fridge, babe.
Sunglasses indoors. Someone in this flat is hiding more than a text.

then.text: Noa tears the end off the challah and eats it standing; Ishai fills the kettle and doesn't switch it on.

moments.text: Noa's phone buzzes in her jacket. She doesn't take it out. Ishai looks at the pocket, then at her.

lines.say: Your pocket is ringing.
It's nobody.
Nobody calls you a lot.
Don't change the subject. We're doing you.
Yesterday you came with a duffel. Then left.
I forgot something. At home.
Then burekas at nine. Then 'dead tired'.
I was dead tired. People get tired.
Noa. You can disappear too. Apparently.
Wow. Okay. Yes, and. Very good, Yael.
I mean it.
Tomorrow. Dinner. Just us. It's about you.
Why is it always about me?
Because you're the one with a barista.
I have to go. My parents. Candles.
Shabbat shalom. Take the challah—
It's yours. Eat something that isn't sad.
Noa. Tomorrow I ask the questions.

commentary.say: Two people telling each other to talk. Neither talking. Classic Friday.
'Tomorrow I ask the questions.' Oh, he's getting brave. Saturday's going to be big.

update.memory: Told Ishai he's apologising by disappearing from Dana. He turned it on me: the phone, the duffel. I said tomorrow's dinner is about him.

beats.goal: Alone before Shabbat. Ishai promised Mrs. Levi not to CALL Eli. So he writes. He finds Eli's number from Tuesday, types a text out loud, deletes 'sorry to bother you', keeps it simple: he is her neighbour from apartment 4, she's well, she misses him and says busy so she doesn't say far, Hanukkah is next week. He sends it. Two grey ticks. He puts the phone face down and sets out the two candles on the counter. No reply yet.
beats.teaser: Ishai promised not to call Eli. He never promised not to write.
beats.forceText: Ishai texts Eli in Toronto, Mrs. Levi's son: she misses him, Hanukkah is next week. Two grey ticks.

forceLines.say: I promised not to call. Nobody said anything about writing.

forceCommentary.say: A legal loophole. From Ishai. Gadi should be nervous.
Two grey ticks. Toronto is seven hours behind. Breathe, everyone.

moments.text: Ishai sits at the desk with his phone, Eli's Toronto number open from Tuesday's call. He types slowly, reading every word aloud to Falafel, and deletes 'sorry to bother you' twice.

lines.say: I promised not to call. Nobody said anything about writing.
'Hi Eli. Ishai, apartment four. Your mother is fine. She misses you. Hanukkah is next week.'

commentary.say: A legal loophole. From Ishai. Gadi should be nervous.
He deleted 'sorry to bother you'. Twice. Lesson four is still working.

moments.text: He sends it. Two grey ticks. He puts the phone face down on the counter, takes two white candles from the drawer and stands them in the old brass holders by the window, next to Moshe.

lines.say: Two grey ticks. Toronto is asleep. Or busy.
Okay. Shabbat. The phone can wait.

commentary.say: Two grey ticks. Toronto is seven hours behind. Breathe, everyone.
Moshe gets a front-row seat to the candles. Again. Nepotism.

beats.goal: Shabbat begins at 16:16. Mrs. Levi knocks with a pot of chicken soup ('you'll eat it, you look thin'); Ishai has Noa's challah and the candles ready. They light the candles together, he says kiddush, they eat at the island. She mentions that Eli used to call every Friday before candles; her own phone stays quiet on the table. Halfway through dinner Ishai's phone buzzes once, face down on the counter. He doesn't look: Shabbat. She notices him not looking and is pleased. She asks about Dana; he says 'busy Friday' and she tells him what she thinks of that. Warm, a little sad, the question left open.
beats.teaser: Candles and soup with Mrs. Levi. A phone buzzes face down.
beats.forceText: Ishai and Mrs. Levi light the Shabbat candles and eat her chicken soup. His phone buzzes once, face down; he leaves it.

forceLines.say: Eli used to call every Friday. Before candles. Like a clock.

forceCommentary.say: The phone buzzed. He didn't look. I'm looking for him. I can't see it.
Soup, candles, a buzzing phone. The Shabbat thriller nobody asked for.

moments.text: Mrs. Levi at the door in her good cardigan with a pot of chicken soup held in a towel. Ishai lets her in; the two candles stand ready by the window and Noa's challah sits under a napkin.

lines.say: Soup. You'll eat it. You look thin.
Shabbat shalom, Mrs. Levi. Come in.
Candles already out. Good boy. Who taught you?
My grandmother. And you, a bit.
Me, a lot. Where's the challah from?
Noa brought it. Sesame.
Noa came and didn't stay?
Her parents. She left fast.
Everybody leaves fast this week.
Matches. Here. You light, I'll hold the plate.
No, you light. It's your house.
Okay. Together, then.
Together. Hands over your eyes. Properly.
Baruch atah...
Amen. Shabbat shalom, motek.
Shabbat shalom.

commentary.say: Candles at sixteen sixteen. Soup at sixteen fifteen. Mrs. Levi is never late.
'Hands over your eyes. Properly.' Even God gets notes from her.

then.text: Ishai pours wine into the kiddush cup and says the blessing over it while Mrs. Levi holds the challah cover with both hands.

moments.text: At the island over two bowls of soup. Mrs. Levi's phone lies by her bowl, dark. Ishai's lies face down on the counter. Falafel waits under the stool for a noodle.

lines.say: Salt?
It's perfect. Don't touch it.
Eli used to call every Friday. Before candles. Like a clock.
Every Friday?
Every. From Toronto it's morning. He'd call from the car.
When did it stop?
It didn't stop. It got... further apart.
Like the visits.
Eat your soup. Don't be clever on Shabbat.
Sorry. Yes. Eating.
Falafel, no. Noodles are for people.
He's half people. Look at his face.
Ha! Like you. Half people, half sorry.
That's harsh, Mrs. Levi.
It's Friday. On Friday I tell the truth.
Only on Friday?
The rest of the week I'm polite.
More soup, then. Polite soup.

commentary.say: 'Half people, half sorry.' Put it on his business card.
Her phone is dark. His is face down. One of those is about to light up.

then.text: Mrs. Levi ladles more soup into his bowl without asking, and Ishai tears the challah in two.

moments.text: Ishai's phone buzzes once on the counter, face down. They both look at it. Ishai turns back to his bowl. Mrs. Levi watches him not look, and smiles into her soup.

lines.say: Your telephone.
It's Shabbat. It can wait.
Look at you. A religious man.
A relaxed one. It can wait one night.
Is it the barista?
I don't know. I'm not looking.
You saw her this week?
I told her I'm busy. Friday.
You're busy? You're eating my soup.
I know. It sounded better in the text.
Motek. 'Busy' is what I say about Eli.
That's different.
It's the same word. I know this word very well.
Mm.
Don't make her say it about you.
Okay.
Okay. Now. Is there dessert in this house?
There's challah. And a very hopeful dog.

commentary.say: The phone buzzed. He didn't look. I'm looking for him. I can't see it.
'I know this word very well.' Mrs. Levi just won the week. Again.

update.memory: Shabbat dinner at Ishai's: we lit the candles together. His phone buzzed and he didn't look. He told the barista 'busy'. I told him what busy means.

hook.text: His phone buzzed once during Shabbat dinner, face down. He didn't look. Was it Eli, or Dana?

previously.text: In class he said 'I want you to stay'. At the bar he texted Dana 'Busy Friday. Sorry.' Tomer read it and called it a cop-out. Noa cancelled, 'dead tired'.

hosts: Friday. Late night out with Tomer. Tomer won at pool and will not stop saying so.
'Busy Friday. Sorry.' That's what he sent Dana. It's Friday. Let's see how busy.
Third day without Cafe Nahat coffee. The moka pot is losing the war.
Avi left Ishai his kiosk keys yesterday and vanished. Today the keys go home.
Shabbat candles at sixteen sixteen. Short Fridays are a sport in this building.
Mrs. Levi said four years yesterday. Four years since Eli came. Ishai promised not to call him.
Note the wording: not to CALL. Ishai has started reading contracts.
Noa brought burekas at nine last night, then cancelled the bar. Sunglasses weather, apparently.
Nap window today: around one. The man has a schedule even for lying down.
Market closes at two on Fridays. If he's cooking, he's racing.
Lior hasn't been near his laptop since Wednesday. Chapter fifteen is still in mourning.
Gadi promised Monday before ten. In writing. Three days to find a new excuse.
Moshe update: aphids down, ego up. Possibly the healthiest one in the flat.
Tomorrow night: PixelPlex. A Midsummer Night's Dream. Tomer, Ishai, and a man with a donkey's head.
Tomorrow after havdalah, dinner with Noa. 'Just us.' She keeps saying that.
Twelve days to the finale. Ten days until Dana answers Haifa. Not that we're counting.
If you're just joining: he likes a barista, the barista might move, he's hiding in his kitchen.
Falafel has walked more this week than Ishai has talked. And Ishai talks to plants.
Clear skies, fourteen degrees at dawn. Ishai will call that cold. Mrs. Levi will call it a robe day.
Fridays on Herzl Street: flowers under every arm and a queue at Avi's.
Remember the flyer he drew yesterday? Watch where it ends up.
Shabbat shalom from the booth. We don't rest. Somebody has to watch.
Mrs. Levi on a Friday is a different woman. Fridays she tells the truth.
Rule of this show: a phone face down is never just a phone.
Kobi says Friday nights at the bar are 'statistically luckier'. Kobi says a lot of things.
radio: Radio Herzl 88.2, Friday morning: flowers, traffic and short tempers. Drive slow, buy tulips.
Candle-lighting in Tel Aviv today at sixteen sixteen. Set your soup accordingly.
A listener asks: is it rude to text 'busy' to someone you like? We'll take calls after the news.
Clear skies all day, fourteen at dawn, twenty-two by lunch. Jacket for the evening.
The market closes at two. If you need coriander, you needed it yesterday.
Next up, a slow one for everyone pretending to be busy this Friday.
Radio Herzl 88.2. If you're cooking, we're the timer. If you're napping, we're the lullaby.
Traffic on the coast road: like a family dinner. Everyone stuck, nobody talking.
Our weekend tip: call your mother. Or your son. Whoever called last, the other one.
That was an old love song about trains. Haifa, three stops. Just saying.
Friday flower prices are up again. Love was never cheap.
Shabbat shalom from the Radio Herzl team. We'll be back after havdalah with the loud stuff.

zelig: Friday. The pigeons know. They eat faster on Fridays.
One duck. Every week, one duck. Loyalty.
A man who goes missing from his own café... the crows talk about that.
Seventeen crumbs. Sixteen. The seventeenth is for Shabbat.
michal: Friday run club at seven. I've heard it went well.
Two more sets and then flowers for my mother.
Short day. Short sets. Same mirror.
sivan: Friday pace. Everybody slows down. Not me.
The hascii guy didn't come today. Too slow even to show up.
lior: Chapter fifteen. A man who stops coming in. That's not a chapter, that's a hole.
She keeps looking at the door. I'm not writing that down. I'm writing it down.
Fridays the café is all flowers and nobody stays.
My hero apologises to his coffee. Lately he doesn't even come to apologise.
kobi: Friday night. My system says double tonight. My system says that every Friday.
Nobody buys a lottery ticket on Shabbat. That's why my numbers win then.
A quiet bar on Friday is a lucky bar. Write it down.
Last week a man left without paying his heart. Ha. Barman, write that one down too.

street: ...tulips or roses, she'll say both are wrong anyway...
...the kiosk guy didn't do the proverb again, is he okay...
...if we leave at four we miss the candles...
...my aunt says the bus stops at three, my aunt is wrong...
market: ...last calls, last calls, two for ten...
...coriander's gone, take parsley, it's a cousin...
...my mother wants fish, my father wants meat, I want to go home...
park: ...he talks to the pigeons, but they listen, have you seen...
...Friday walk, then soup, then sleep for a week...
...the duck has a name, I swear, the old man knows it...
cafe: ...she asked twice if the quiet guy came in...
...a basil leaf on the foam, that's a whole language...
...Haifa? Who goes to Haifa for coffee...
...closing at two, Shabbat, take it to go...

chat.say: Reminder: stair light fund is complete. Thank you all. Moti says no more coins, please.
Who took the yellow bucket from the roof? It's mine. Since 1998.
Bucket is with me, washing the bus mats. Back by noon. Boaz.
Anyone have a spare challah cover? Ours went to the laundry.
I have three. Come knock. Not after four.
Please don't leave flowers on the stairs, the cats eat them. Moti.
Soup for anyone who wants. Big pot. Bring your own bowl.
Shabbat shalom to the whole building. Candles at 16:16.
